name: Gặp nhau ở giữa
notes: chapters = seconds in film.mp4 where the film waits for a tap, taken from scene.html by stops.py: the title frame, one stop in each of the five beats (PAUSE.inBeat into its beat), the climax (PAUSE.climax: the two planes touching inside the postmark) and the last frame (the planes unfolded into one blank sheet). Each sits a quarter of a frame into its frame, so a seek shows that frame and round(t * fps) finds its boxes. hints = the scene's own words at those stops (WORDS.cue, ui.next, WORDS.hint, ui.skip); a card can override them with "chapters". reveal = null: no 3D envelope; after the last stop a tap opens the letter. slots.json: cap0-k ... cap4-k are the beats' titles after their number (label; the number "01 ·" stays in the film), cap0-l ... cap4-l their lines (caption), on the airmail slips that slide up and away; city-hers and city-mine the two cities' names under their dots (label, fading with the cities as the camera closes in); middle the place where the planes meet (label). Compromises: one film serves every card, so the map, the route, the distance, the degree labels, the scale bar and the compass are drawn for the scene's own two cities (Hà Nội to Đà Nẵng, 606 km); a card can rename the cities but not move them, and the kilometre counter in the corner (part of the HUD) is not in the film. The postmark's arcs held the meeting place and the day she opens it; curved words cannot be painted on, so the arcs carry the scene's own "Gặp nhau ở giữa" and "Thư máy bay" and the card's place is painted in a straight line under the stamp. The words are painted over the film, so a city's name shows on top of the plane that sits on it at the start. The letter is live HTML in the player, so the film ends on the blank sheet the planes unfold into. fonts = the faces the player paints these slots in (latin, latin-ext and vietnamese).
